newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast to meet donors on 3-yr economic plan.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast to meet donors on 3-yr economic plan.

text.p: Ivory Coast will meet IMF and World Bank officials from August 8-15 to discuss an economic policy framework for the next three years, donors said.

"It is a joint mission between the IMF and the World Bank so we can agree a policy framework paper which will be in the government's economic policy for the next three years," World Bank head of mission in Ivory Coast Shigeo Katsu told Reuters.
"We need to agree during the August mission (from Washington) the three year overall programme," Katsu said.
Items up for discussion included poverty reduction, social issues and commodities policy.
"The IMF will also come up with measures for the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility," he added.
Elements of that would be looked at by the World Bank in considering new structural adjustment credits arising each year, he said.

Structural adjustment credits in place include a $150 million agriculture sector loan from the World Bank dating to 1995. Terms include liberalisation of marketing of the country's main export commodities, including cocoa and coffee.
Ivory Coast is the world's largest producer of cocoa -- accounting for 40 percent of global production.
It is keen to diversify its rural economy by promoting food processing, mining and energy, and to add more value to exports.
The economy suffered a setback after devaluation of its CFA franc currency in 1994 but the government has forecast eight percent growth for 1997.
